feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
Assuming each signature is consistently 65 witness bytes offers a straightforward approach, simplifying calculations and reducing complexity. In situations where a shorter signature is presented, the system benefits from improved transaction prioritization due to the reduced size. This method introduces only a minimal error margin of approximately 0.25 virtual bytes per signature, which remains negligible in most practical scenarios.
A further consideration involves determining whether all valid witnesses conform to a specific weight range. Establishing such a proof would ensure predictable resource allocation and network efficiency, enhancing the reliability of signature handling. The suggestion to use "DEPTH 2 NUMNOTEQUAL" is noted as potentially being a more self-evident or intuitive solution within this context.
This discussion underlines the trade-offs between procedural simplicity and theoretical rigor when accounting for witness sizes and their corresponding impact on transaction processing.
